findings.issue: FR-HOST-001/002 not met: when there is no Codex session (non-Codex host), the private session-event command throws and exits 1 instead of returning a structured unavailable response and exiting normally. The catch block treats every error as fail-loud, so missing-session falls into the same path as real parameter/material/identity errors.
findings.recommendation: Detect a missing session before other validation and emit a JSON result like { status: 'unavailable', reason: 'no bound Codex session' } with exit 0; reserve exit 1 and stack traces for genuine parameter/material/identity failures.

findings.issue: FR-ANALYZE-001/002 are only partially implemented. The four convergence checks (requirement coverage, goal achievement, acceptance clarity, solution convergence) and the build-spec contract comparison are evaluated inside the make-decision / build-spec stage handlers, not inside the spec-analyze profile that stage-runtime uses for record-spec-analyze. validateStageSpecAnalyzeProfile still only validates materials, evidence bindings, and generic coverage rows.
findings.recommendation: Either extend STAGE_SPEC_ANALYZE_PROFILES / validateStageSpecAnalyzeProfile with stage-specific operational checks for make-decision and build-spec, or record an explicit incomplete evidence note explaining why the profile intentionally delegates to stage handlers and how the delegation preserves independent verifiability.

findings.issue: FR-CONV-002 is only surface-checked. The function looks for a requirement-matrix section heading but does not verify the five required coverage dimensions (业务目标/未来扩展影响/UI交互/验收目标/影响范围) or per-row disposition. The originalRequirement parameter is also unused by the caller, so an unprocessed original requirement cannot be detected.
findings.recommendation: Add structural checks that the matrix contains the five dimension labels and that every original/追加 requirement row has a covered/deferred/rejected disposition; pass the original requirement list from the stage handler so the check can report gaps instead of only section presence.

findings.line_or_region: working tree relative to plan.md / tasks.md
findings.issue: Several files that the plan says must be modified are unchanged or missing: workflows/make-decision/SKILL.md, skills/spec-clarify/SKILL.md, skills/spec-analyze/SKILL.md, tools/cli/task-bootstrap.mjs, CONTEXT.md, tests/contract/spec-analyze-completeness.test.mjs, tests/contract/task-bootstrap-integrity.test.mjs, tests/contract/governance-startup-event-early-failure.test.mjs. As a result, large parts of the spec are not covered by the current changes (FR-CONV-001/004 end-card and make-decision contract, FR-CLARIFY-001/002 spec-clarify contract, FR-AUTHORING-001/002 build-spec writing discipline, FR-TASK-001/002 bootstrap semantics, FR-HOST-001/002/004 host/worktree handling, FR-REVIEW-001/002/003 delivery path, FR-DOG-001 dogfood signals).
findings.recommendation: Either complete the planned file changes, or update plan.md and tasks.md to record the reduced scope and move the remaining FR/AC to a follow-up task with explicit evidence; do not treat the current subset as a full build-code implementation.

findings.issue: The usage string advertises public commands run|review|verify|confirm|authorize, but the internal allowed command set uses review-risk-pause, capture-tests, artifact, authorize-operation, etc. The mismatch can mislead callers about what stage-runtime.mjs accepts directly.
findings.recommendation: Align the usage text with the actual internal command names, or document the public-to-internal mapping so the help string is not taken as the direct CLI surface.

findings.issue: The new regression test only exercises the P1 convergence / Clarify / Grill seams. It does not cover the spec-analyze convergence checks, non-Codex host degradation, task/bootstrap semantics, review delivery, authoring discipline, or dogfood six-signal verification described in the spec.
findings.recommendation: Add the planned P2/P3 contract tests before declaring build-code complete, or record the missing coverage as incomplete evidence in the task's quality facts.

summary: The current changes implement the P1 convergence/Clarify/Grill seams and the new regression test passes, but they leave major parts of the spec unaddressed: the spec-analyze profile does not check the four convergence dimensions or build-spec contract comparison, the five-dimension coverage matrix is not verified, the session-event command fails loudly instead of degrading for non-Codex hosts, and several files that the plan says must be modified are absent. The build-code work therefore has actionable spec gaps and cannot be judged clean.
